title: Fireworks sale ban and Kraus Lands sale approved
subtitle: Waterloo also approved a Roy Schmidt Road subdivision, designated five festivals, and urged stimulus funding amid tariffs.
overview: Council approved a package of fireworks changes {{vote:m4}}. Fireworks use will be limited to the day of each holiday (two days for Diwali/Deepavali), sales in Waterloo will be prohibited from January 2026, and administrative penalties will increase. Staff will return with an updated by-law and fine schedule, and an education campaign is planned. Fireworks will still be available to buy online with proof of age.

Council also approved the sale of the Former Kraus Lands to Urban Legend Developments Ltd. for $33,500,000, naming it the preferred proponent. After a public meeting, it approved a zone change and draft plan of subdivision for 550 Roy Schmidt Road and 558 Conservation Drive. Staff said construction depends on planned road and pumping station work nearby.

Council designated five 2025 Significant Festivals and Events for by-law exemptions, and called on federal and provincial governments for municipal stimulus funding in response to tariffs. Council had met in closed session earlier in the day, and the minutes report no public decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved limiting fireworks to the day of the holiday, banning their sale in Waterloo from January 2026, and increasing administrative penalties.
Council named Urban Legend Developments Ltd. the preferred proponent and approved selling the lands to it for $33,500,000, with the Mayor and Clerk authorized to sign the agreement.

decisions.item: Roy Schmidt Road and Conservation Drive subdivision
decisions.detail: Council approved the zone change and draft plan of subdivision for the site, delegated certain approval powers to the Director of Planning, and extended the deadline for replacement dwelling permits to September 9, 2030.
Council designated five 2025 events for by-law exemptions: the Busker Carnival, Royal Medieval Faire, Kultrun World Music Festival, Afro Fest and Uptown Waterloo Jazz Festival.
Council called on federal and provincial governments to fund municipal infrastructure, housing and transit stimulus, and to send the resolution to municipal associations, MPPs, MPs and ministers.

debate: On fireworks, supporters cited complaints about noise, effects on animals and wildlife, litter in parks, and use at all hours. One councillor said the changes would still allow responsible use while limiting easy access.

One councillor opposed the fireworks recommendations, saying the survey was not statistically significant, results were mixed, and difficult enforcement is not a reason to limit sales. Staff said the sale ban was meant to curb impulse purchases and align with neighbouring municipalities.

On festival exemptions, a councillor asked why events supported by the downtown business association were not on the list. Staff said the report covers only affiliated organizations under the festivals policy, and other events can request exemptions separately.

A resident delegate opposed the subdivision, citing density, effects on conservation areas and wildlife, and traffic safety for children. Staff said transit funding is a draft plan condition, the lands are outside the conservation authority's regulation area, and the plan follows the district plan.
On the Kraus Lands, councillors asked about engagement with First Nations. Staff said it has focused on environmental and archaeological work and will continue as development concepts advance.
